name: Kṛṣṇa
summary: In U06's texts: speaker of the Uddhava Gītā (Bhāgavata 11.7-29), in which he gives Uddhava his final teaching before leaving the world, and of the Uttara Gītā; he quotes the Kāma Gītā (Mahābhārata 14.13).

name: Uddhava
summary: Kṛṣṇa's cousin, counsellor and devotee; recipient of the Uddhava Gītā. Earlier Kṛṣṇa sent him to Vraja, where he learned from the gopīs' love (Bhāgavata 10.46-47). At the end of the teaching he departs for Badarikāśrama (11.29).

realization_account.text: Having heard the teaching, Uddhava, freed of doubt, went to Badarikāśrama to live it out (Bhāgavata 11.29).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Kapila
summary: In U06's texts: the avatāra Kapila, son of Kardama and Devahūti, who teaches his mother a devotional Sāṃkhya (Kapila Gītā, Bhāgavata 3.25-33). The Bhāgavata identifies him with the founder of Sāṃkhya ('tattva-saṅkhyātā', 3.24-25); some later authors distinguish the two Kapilas.

name: Devahūti
summary: Daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu, wife of the sage Kardama and mother of Kapila; the questioner of the Kapila Gītā, who asks for a devotion suited to her and attains liberation.

realization_account.text: Following her son's instruction she practised devotional yoga at Bindusaras, her body withered unnoticed, and she attained the Lord; the place became Siddhapada (Bhāgavata 3.33).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Dattātreya
summary: Son of Atri and Anasūyā, counted the sixth avatāra in the Bhāgavata (1.3.11: he taught ānvīkṣikī to Alarka, Prahlāda and others); Yadu and the Haihayas gained yogic powers from him (2.7.4). The tradition identifies him with the unnamed avadhūta who teaches King Yadu his twenty-four teachers (Bhāgavata 11.7-9), and ascribes to him the Avadhūta Gītā and the Jīvanmukta Gītā. Revered as the ādiguru of the Datta tradition and in the Nāth lineages.

name: Yadu
summary: Ancestor-king of the Yādavas who questions a carefree young avadhūta brāhmaṇa about the source of his peace and hears of his twenty-four teachers (Bhāgavata 11.7.25-11.9.33).

realization_account.text: Hearing the avadhūta, Yadu became free of all attachment and even-minded (Bhāgavata 11.9.33).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Piṅgalā
summary: A courtesan of Videha whose sudden disenchantment while waiting for clients makes her one of the avadhūta's teachers (Bhāgavata 11.8.22-44) and the singer of the Piṅgalā Gītā (Mahābhārata 12.168.46-52): 'hope is the greatest misery, hopelessness the greatest happiness'.

realization_account.text: Waiting through the night for a rich lover, she felt deep disgust, turned to the Self as her true beloved and slept happily, free of expectation.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Bodhya
summary: A tranquil sage who, questioned by King Nahuṣa, names six teachers: Piṅgalā, the osprey, the snake, the bee, the arrow-maker and the maiden (Mahābhārata 12.171.57-61).

name: Maṅki
summary: Singer of the Maṅki Gītā (Mahābhārata 12.171), who renounced desire after his efforts at wealth failed. A Maṅki is also taught by Vasiṣṭha in the Mokṣopāya's Nirvāṇa book (MU 6.180-183; identity of the two not asserted).

name: Purūravas (Aila)
summary: King, son of Iḍā, infatuated with the apsaras Urvaśī; his song of disenchantment is the Aila Gītā (Bhāgavata 11.26).

name: Sanaka
summary: Eldest of the four mind-born sons of Brahmā (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, Sanatkumāra), whose question on separating mind from the guṇas occasions the Haṃsa Gītā (Bhāgavata 11.13).

name: Haṃsa (the Lord as swan)
summary: The form of a swan in which the Lord appeared before Brahmā and the Kumāras to answer their question (Bhāgavata 11.13.19-42).

name: Aṣṭāvakra
summary: A sage born bent in eight places by his father Kahoḍa's curse; as a boy he defeated Bandin at Janaka's court (Mahābhārata 3.132-134). The Aṣṭāvakra Gītā presents him as Janaka's teacher of non-dual knowledge.

name: Janaka
summary: In U06's texts: King of Videha who receives Aṣṭāvakra's teaching and voices his awakening (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā ch. 2 and later chapters); overhears the Siddhas' songs and awakens (Yoga Vāsiṣṭha 5.8-10); his verse 'my wealth is endless, for nothing is mine; if Mithilā burns, nothing of mine burns' is quoted in Mahābhārata 12.171.56.

realization_account.text: On hearing Aṣṭāvakra he exclaims that he is stainless, peaceful consciousness beyond nature, long deceived by delusion (Aṣṭāvakra Gītā 2.1); in the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha he awakens through the Siddha Gītā and rules as one liberated while living.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Ṛbhu
summary: A mind-born son of Brahmā, knower of reality from birth, teacher of Nidāgha (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.15-16, verified); in the Śivarahasya he teaches Nidāgha the Ṛbhu Gītā received from Śiva.

name: Nidāgha
summary: Son of Pulastya and disciple of Ṛbhu, who lived at Vīranagara on the Devikā; Ṛbhu returns twice in disguise to test and teach him (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.15-16); the recipient of the Ṛbhu Gītā.

name: Śiva
summary: In U06's texts: speaker of the Īśvara Gītā (to the sages), the Śiva Gītā (to Rāma), the Guru Gītā (to Pārvatī) and the Rudra Gītā (to the Pracetās); narrator of the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa to Pārvatī; in the Mokṣopāya he teaches Vasiṣṭha the true worship of the divine as consciousness (MU 6.31-46).

name: Pārvatī
summary: Śiva's consort, the questioner in the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa (her doubt why the supreme Rāma grieved for Sītā, 1.1.13-15) and in the Guru Gītā; in Śākta texts identified with the Goddess who herself teaches (Devī Gītā, Bhagavatī Gītā).

name: The Goddess (Devī)
summary: The supreme Goddess, appearing as Bhuvaneśvarī, who teaches Himālaya and the gods in the Devī Gītā (Devī Bhāgavata 7.31-40): she is consciousness, supreme Brahman, whose power is māyā.

name: Himavat (Himālaya)
summary: King of the mountains and father of Pārvatī, who asks the Goddess for the yoga, devotion and knowledge that lead to her (Devī Gītā).

name: Gaṇeśa (Gajānana)
summary: The elephant-faced lord who, in the Gaṇeśa Purāṇa, teaches King Vareṇya the Gaṇeśa Gītā.

name: Vareṇya
summary: The king to whom Gajānana teaches the Gaṇeśa Gītā; in the Gaṇeśa Purāṇa Gaṇeśa had been born in his house.

name: Vasiṣṭha
summary: In U06's texts: the family priest of the Ikṣvākus who, at Viśvāmitra's request, teaches the despondent young Rāma the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha / Mokṣopāya; within it he recounts his own learning from Brahmā, from the crow Bhuśuṇḍa and from Śiva.

name: Rāma
summary: In U06's texts: the student of Vasiṣṭha in the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha (whose first book records his dispassion at sixteen); the teacher of Hanumān (Rāma-hṛdaya), Lakṣmaṇa (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa 3.4 and the Rāma Gītā), Śabarī (the nine means of devotion) and Vibhīṣaṇa (Rāmcaritmānas); in the Śiva Gītā the recipient of Śiva's teaching. The Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa presents him as the supreme Brahman.

realization_account.text: In the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha Rāma, after Vasiṣṭha's teaching, rests in the supreme state (Nirvāṇa-prakaraṇa, opening chapters, e.g. MU 6.5 'rāghava-viśrānti'); the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa instead treats him as the Lord who never lost knowledge.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Vālmīki
summary: In U06's texts: the traditional author of the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha / Mokṣopāya, who opens it by telling Bharadvāja that Brahmā sent him to complete a Rāmāyaṇa of liberation (MU 1.1).

name: Viśvāmitra
summary: In U06's texts: the sage whose request for Rāma's help occasions the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha and who is present throughout Vasiṣṭha's teaching.

name: Sītā
summary: In the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa she instructs Hanumān (1.1.31-43): Rāma is the non-dual Brahman and she is primal nature (mūlaprakṛti), the agent of all the deeds superimposed on him.

name: Hanumān
summary: In the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa the devoted servant judged fit for knowledge, to whom Sītā and Rāma teach the Rāma-hṛdaya (1.1.29-52).

name: Lakṣmaṇa
summary: Rāma's brother: recipient of Rāma's teaching on māyā, knowledge and devotion (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa 3.4) and of the Rāma Gītā (7.5); in the Rāmcaritmānas he himself teaches Guha (the Lakṣmaṇa Gītā).

name: Śabarī
summary: A forest woman of low birth, disciple of the sage Mataṅga, who waited for Rāma; he teaches her that gender, caste and stage of life are no cause of devotion and gives her the nine means of devotion (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa 3.10).

realization_account.text: After guiding Rāma to Sugrīva she entered the fire before him and, freed of all bonds made by ignorance, attained liberation by Rāma's grace (AR 3.10.39-42).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Vibhīṣaṇa
summary: Rāvaṇa's righteous brother who took refuge with Rāma; the Rāmcaritmānas's 'chariot of dharma' teaching is addressed to him.

name: Bhuśuṇḍa
summary: The ancient crow living on a wish-fulfilling tree on a peak of Meru, who tells Vasiṣṭha how contemplation of the breath (prāṇa-cintā) made him outlive many world-ages (Mokṣopāya 6.14-27; Yoga Vāsiṣṭha Nirvāṇa, pūrvārdha). The Rāmcaritmānas's Kāk Bhuśuṇḍi is a related figure.

realization_account.text: Resting in the Self through contemplation of the breath, he remains unaffected by the dissolutions of the worlds he has witnessed.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Cūḍālā
summary: Queen of Mālava who attained self-knowledge by her own inquiry and powers through breath-discipline; unable to teach her husband Śikhidhvaja as herself, she came to him in the forest disguised as the young brāhmaṇa Kumbha and led him to realization (Mokṣopāya 6.81-114; Yoga Vāsiṣṭha Nirvāṇa, pūrvārdha).

realization_account.text: Through daily inquiry into what the self is she found the Self and 'shone' so that her husband remarked on her changed radiance (MU 6.82-83 'cūḍālā-prabodha', 'cūḍālātmalābha').
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Śikhidhvaja
summary: King of Mālava who renounced his kingdom for forest austerities but found no peace until his wife Cūḍālā, disguised as Kumbha, taught him that renunciation of everything includes renunciation of the mind that renounces.

realization_account.text: After giving up even his ascetic's belongings and his body-identification he entered a long samādhi, awoke liberated and returned to rule with Cūḍālā.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Līlā
summary: Queen who, grieving for her husband Padma, is taught by the goddess Sarasvatī (Jñapti) and shown in consciousness-body the worlds of her husband's past and future lives (Yoga Vāsiṣṭha 3.15-60).

name: Prahlāda
summary: In U06's texts: the asura king who realizes the Self through his own inquiry and Viṣṇu's grace and remains in long samādhi until awakened by Viṣṇu to rule (Yoga Vāsiṣṭha 5.30-43); he questions the python-vow sage (Mahābhārata 12.172).

name: Bali
summary: In the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha (5.22-29), the asura king who remembers his father Virocana's teaching on the realm beyond the worlds, inquires, and attains self-knowledge while continuing to rule.

name: Dharmavyādha
summary: The righteous meat-seller of Mithilā who teaches the proud brāhmaṇa Kauśika the dharma of one's own station and of service to parents (Mahābhārata 3.198-206).

name: Abhinanda (Gauḍa Abhinanda)
summary: Kashmiri author to whom the Laghu Yoga Vāsiṣṭha is ascribed.

name: Bhāskarakaṇṭha
summary: Kashmiri Paṇḍit, author of the Mokṣopāyaṭīkā and (outside U06) of the Bhāskarī commentary on Abhinavagupta's Īśvarapratyabhijñāvimarśinī.

name: Ānandabodhendra Sarasvatī
summary: Author of the Tātparyaprakāśa commentary on the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha.

name: Ātmasukha
summary: Recalled as author of the Vāsiṣṭhacandrikā on the Laghu Yoga Vāsiṣṭha.

name: Nīlakaṇṭha Caturdhara
summary: Seventeenth-century Mahārāṣṭrian scholar in Vārāṇasī, famous for his Mahābhārata commentary; in U06 the commentator on the Gaṇeśa Gītā.

name: Vyāsa
summary: In U06's texts: the traditional author of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa (Uddhava and Kapila Gītās), the Devī Bhāgavata (Devī Gītā), the Kūrma Purāṇa and, as part of the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa; the speaker of the Vyāsa Gītā.

name: Yama
summary: Lord of death; in U06's texts the speaker of the Yama Gītās (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.7; Narasiṃha Purāṇa 8; Agni Purāṇa 381, the last addressed to Naciketas).

name: Naciketas
summary: In U06's texts: the addressee of the Agni Purāṇa's Yama Gītā, which retells the Kaṭha Upaniṣad teaching.

name: Parāśara
summary: In U06's texts: the sage who instructs King Janaka in the Parāśara Gītā (Mahābhārata 12.279-287).

name: Tulsīdās
summary: In U06's texts: author of the Rāmcaritmānas passages known as the Lakṣmaṇa Gītā and the Vibhīṣaṇa Gītā; he drew on the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa (Śiva-Pārvatī frame, Śabarī's nine devotions).

name: Eknāth
summary: In U06's texts: author of the Eknāthī Bhāgavata, the Marathi commentary on the Uddhava Gītā (Bhāgavata Book 11).

name: Vidyāraṇya
summary: In U06's context: his Jīvanmuktiviveka builds its account of liberation while living largely on quotations from the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha (e.g. the weakening of latent tendencies and the dissolution of mind).

name: Gauḍapāda
summary: In U06's context: a commentary on the Uttara Gītā is ascribed to him (attribution doubtful).

name: Ramana Maharshi
summary: In U06's context (recent reception): recommended the Ṛbhu Gītā, which was read aloud in his presence, and quoted the Yoga Vāsiṣṭha and the Aṣṭāvakra Gītā.

name: Vivekananda
summary: In U06's context (recent reception): he often quoted the Avadhūta Gītā and the Aṣṭāvakra Gītā; Ramakrishna is remembered as having had him read the Aṣṭāvakra Saṃhitā.

name: Muktananda
summary: In U06's context (recent reception): made the Guru Gītā the daily morning chant of his ashrams (Ganeshpuri recension).
